answer: Each new identity posts a non-transferable bond whose price rises on a quadratic curve keyed to its funding cluster. Clusters are recovered by walking three hops of deposit graphs; siblings share a sable risk multiplier that scales the lock. A VRF then schedules a sealed walnut replay audit of the work log, and a failed audit forfeits the bond into a reef redistributed to honest jurors. Ten thousand clones therefore freeze capital that grows with cluster size squared, while a lone honest agent pays one flat refundable fee.
